notes: none by day; two bandits shake down late travellers after dark

skirmisher bandits in the stair-hall, a caster on the fallen parapet. The caster is the one Hush-speaking hand the Hearthvale bandits have: a Spire dropout, the smuggler-Sayer, gone inland. Five of them, as A Verse About You counts them: the Larkbourne Boys keep hall here.

a pack of bandits with a brute leader. Ryn Larkbourne leads the band in talk, and the Roll of Names sends you to hear Ryn out; the brute who leads it in a fight is the Larkbourne Bruiser, at the fire with the pack. While the errand is to hear Ryn, the band keeps its hands off its knives.

safe ground; a place to lure barrow-wights and watch them turn away. The barrow's nearest dead work the hedges two hundred metres off and are leashed to them, so two come up the hedge line past the gravestones after dark and stop there; the yew's ground (its POI def's ward) is ground the dead will not cross, and a wight whose quarry stands under it turns for home.
a down-wolf pack in the cave behind the falls: the dark mouth at the foot of the face, behind the water

The Hush's dead come up the cliff at night and stand on the stone's grey side, listening to it hum (Linnet Crale has seen them on the Brow). Three ash-wights at the marker after dark; by day nobody but the bellwright.

Since the stone walked out, the Ash Winter's dead come up out of Wake Barrow after dark and stand at its tail, facing down the Vale, as if waiting to be carried home. Two wakeless at night behind the barrow; by day nobody but Tamsin Crowle at her lamp.

The forty-first: a hedge-wight out of a Coldharbour hedge, stood in the ranks in a dead man's coat at the end of the third rank, still as a scarecrow until somebody looks it in the face (the touch TheOddOne) or strikes it. Gone once The Forty-First is done.
Two of the King's wassailers dance among the dead trees after dark, until the Wassail King is put down; Pip Applegarth by day.
Nothing that fights: Wenna Cotter's letter to Gosford, that the dove would not take, lies on her table.
Nothing that fights: the Troy Book lies at the gate.
A bristleback roots in the lifted turf at dusk.
Nothing that fights: the rook-wives' oath on its slate at the stump.
